articleinfo.title: NGINX JS DOM — Header and Body Filters

section.title: Overview
section.simpara: NGINX JS DOM lets JavaScript code intercept and transform every HTTP response that passes through a location. The interception happens at two points in nginx’s filter chain:

listitem.simpara: Header filters — called once, just before response headers are sent to the client. The callback receives the live NginxRequest object and may mutate response headers in place. The filter is always synchronous.

Body filters — called for each piece of the response body (streaming modes) or once on the complete body (whole-body modes). Four execution modes cover every combination of sync/async and chunk/whole: wholeBodySync, wholeBodyAsync, streamingSync, streamingAsync.

section.simpara: Filters are registered per-location via methods on the NginxLocation object (accessible through nginx.http.servers[i].locations[j] or by iterating nginx.http.servers[i].locations). Registering a filter from any script that runs at config time — js_source, js_init_http, js_preprocess — is sufficient; the filter then applies to every request that reaches that location.

section.simpara: All filter management methods live on the NginxLocation object.

section.programlisting: location.addBodyFilter(mode, fn) location.addBodyFilter(mode, fn, opts)

entry.simpara: Synchronous whole-body transform. Signature: function(req, body) → string | undefined body is the complete accumulated response body as a string. Return a new string to replace it; return undefined (or any non-string) to pass through unchanged.

Asynchronous whole-body transform. Signature: async function(req, body) → Promise<string | undefined> Same semantics as wholeBodySync but the function may await I/O or timers before returning. If the Promise rejects, the connection is closed with an error.

Synchronous per-chunk transform. Signature: function(req, chunk, flags) Called once per nginx body-filter call (one "chunk"). Output is emitted via req.sendBuffer(data) — any number of calls per invocation. If sendBuffer is never called the chunk is dropped (not forwarded).

Asynchronous per-chunk transform. Signature: async function(req, chunk, flags) → Promise<string | undefined> Called once per nginx body-filter call. The chunk is transformed via the resolved value of the returned Promise: a string replaces the chunk; '' drops it; undefined (or any non-string) passes the original chunk through. If the Promise rejects, the connection is closed with an error.

section.title: location.headerFilters (getter)
section.simpara: Returns a snapshot array of { name, priority, fn } objects for all currently registered header filters, in dispatch order.

section.title: location.bodyFilters (getter)
section.simpara: Returns a snapshot array of { name, priority, fn, mode } objects for all currently registered body filters, in dispatch order.

section.title: Filter options object
section.simpara: Both addHeaderFilter and addBodyFilter accept an optional second/third opts argument that controls where the new filter is inserted in the list:
section.programlisting: { name: string, // symbolic name — used by remove/get priority: number, // lower = earlier; default 50 before: fn | string, // insert immediately before this filter after: fn | string, // insert immediately after this filter index: number // insert at this absolute position (0-based) }
section.simpara: Precedence (highest first): index > before / after > priority.
If before or after references a filter that does not exist, the new filter is appended.

section.title: Header filter API
section.simpara: A header filter receives a single NginxRequest argument. At that point response headers are still mutable. Use standard property access on req:

Header filters are always synchronous. async function callbacks are accepted but any awaited operation completes after headers are already sent — do not rely on async behaviour inside a header filter.
The return value is ignored.

section.title: Whole-body modes (wholeBodySync, wholeBodyAsync)
section.simpara: The body is accumulated from all nginx chain links until last_buf is seen. Then the JS filter chain runs once on the complete body string.
Chaining: when multiple whole-body filters are registered they run in registration order; each filter receives the output of the previous one as its body argument.

section.title: Streaming modes (streamingSync, streamingAsync)
section.simpara: Streaming filters run on each chunk individually as nginx delivers it. The filter chain processes chunks in registration order.

Output is produced via req.sendBuffer(data). Multiple calls per invocation are allowed; their output is concatenated in call order and forwarded downstream. The next filter in the chain receives the concatenated output of the previous filter — not the original chunk.
flags is an object with one property:

listitem.simpara: flags.last — true if this is the last chunk (corresponds to nginx’s last_buf flag).

section.title: Mode selection (Mode A vs Mode B)
section.simpara: nginx JS DOM uses two internal dispatch strategies based on what filter types are registered for a location:

entry.simpara: nginx body-filter calls pass directly to the streaming chain; the body is never accumulated. Each call to nginx’s body filter = one call to each streaming filter.
Location has at least one wholeBody* filter
The body is fully accumulated, then ALL filters run in registration order on the complete body. streamingSync/streamingAsync filters in this list receive the whole body as a single last chunk.

section.simpara: The mode is selected automatically based on the filter list at request time. There is no explicit configuration knob.

section.title: Mixed mode (Mode B with streaming filters)
section.simpara: When both wholeBody* and streaming* filters share a location, Mode B is used and all filters run in registration order on the accumulated body. Streaming filters behave as follows:

listitem.simpara: streamingSync: called with (req, body, {last: true}). Emit output via req.sendBuffer(); no call → body is dropped.
streamingAsync: called with (req, body, {last: true}). Resolved string replaces the body; undefined passes through; '' drops it.

section.title: Execution order and chaining
section.simpara: Filters execute in the order they appear in the location’s filter list. Both header and body filter lists are independent.

section.title: Dynamic filter management
section.simpara: Filters can be added and removed at runtime from within a running filter callback. The implementation uses copy-on-write (COW) for the filter list: mutations during dispatch do not affect the current iteration but take effect for the next request.

section.title: Priority and ordering
section.simpara: Filters added without an explicit index, before, or after option are inserted based on priority (lower = earlier, default 50):

entry.simpara: Exception is logged; body is passed through unchanged; next filter runs.
Error is logged; connection is closed (HTTP 500 or connection reset).
Exception is logged; chunk is dropped; next filter runs.
Error is logged; connection is closed.
addBodyFilter / addHeaderFilter called with wrong type
TypeError is thrown immediately (synchronous, propagates to the caller).
